title: Remove openSessions calls from village_spawn/village_wake
description:
## Context

`village_spawn` and `village_wake` currently call `client.tui.openSessions()` with the intent of helping users find spawned worker/overseer sessions. However, those sessions are **child sessions** (created with `parentID`), and the `/sessions` view only lists **root sessions**. This means the spawned village sessions never appear in the dialog that opens, making the feature misleading and broken.

Users report: "I don't see any of the sessions that village spawns!"

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`fix/village-orphans-report`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Remove all `openSessions: true` default behavior from `village_spawn` and `village_wake`.
- [ ] Remove the `openSessions` parameter entirely from both tools (it's not useful if the sessions don't appear).
- [ ] Update toast messages to stop mentioning `/sessions` or `ctrl+x l` for finding village sessions.
- [ ] Update toast messages to clearly explain how to navigate to child sessions: `ctrl+x right/left` (cycle children) and `ctrl+x up` (back to parent).
- [ ] Update `VILLAGE.md` to remove `/sessions (ctrl+x l)` references for village navigation; replace with child-navigation keybinds.
- [ ] Update `agents/mayor.md` to remove `/sessions (ctrl+x l)` references for village navigation; replace with child-navigation keybinds.
- [ ] Verify the tool output text in `village_spawn` and `village_wake` no longer mentions "Session selector: opened" or similar.

## Notes

This is a UX fix: the feature exists but is completely non-functional for its stated purpose. Better to remove it than confuse users.

Fallback for users who want direct access: they can run `opencode --session <sessionID>` with the printed session IDs.

title: Add /village:orphans command (detect/fix unassigned open beads)
description:
## Context

Sometimes beads are left open without an assignee (or assigned to an unexpected role), which causes the village work loop to miss them. We want a quick command `/village:orphans` that reports these cases and (optionally) assigns them to the right role.

Because `:` in filenames is not portable, implement the command in `opencode.json` `command` config.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/village-kick-command`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/village:orphans` exists as a custom command.
- [ ] Running it produces a concise report of:
  - open + in_progress non-epic beads with missing assignee
  - open + in_progress beads assigned outside {worker, overseer} (e.g. mayor/other)
- [ ] Optional `fix` mode assigns missing-assignee beads using a safe heuristic.
- [ ] Docs mention `/village:orphans` and how to use `fix`.

## Notes

Heuristic default for fix mode:
- Ignore epics.
- If title/description suggests review/verification (keywords like review, verify, checks, overseer), assign to overseer; otherwise assign to worker.

title: Implement /village:orphans command (opencode.json)
description:
## Context

Add `/village:orphans` command in `opencode.json`.

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/village-kick-command`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `opencode.json` adds `command[\"village:orphans\"]` with description.
- [ ] Command behavior:
  - Collect open + in_progress beads via `bd list --status open --json` and `bd list --status in_progress --json`.
  - Identify "orphans": non-epic issues where `assignee` is empty/missing.
  - Identify "suspect assignees": issues where `assignee` is present but not `worker` or `overseer`.
  - Print a short report: counts + up to ~20 items with `id`, `title`, `status`, and current assignee.
- [ ] Args:
  - `/village:orphans` => report only
  - `/village:orphans fix` => perform `bd update <id> --assignee <worker|overseer>` for orphans only
- [ ] Fix heuristic:
  - Ignore epics.
  - If title/description contains keywords: `review|verify|verification|check|checks|overseer|approve`, assign `overseer`.
  - Else assign `worker`.
- [ ] If `bd` is unavailable or no `.beads` DB exists, report that gracefully and exit.

## Notes

Keep it safe: never reassign already-assigned issues automatically; `fix` only touches truly-unassigned ones.

title: Deterministic Village Workflow (no LLM drift)
description:
## Context

The current Agentic Village workflow relies on LLMs to correctly and consistently:
- create child beads for an epic
- assign beads to `worker` vs `overseer`
- claim the next bead to work

This sometimes drifts (missing tickets, wrong assignee, or multiple beads claimed at once).

Goal: move critical workflow transitions into deterministic code in `plugins/village.ts` (tools), so the workflow is consistent and enforceable.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/deterministic-village-workflow`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Mayor can deterministically scaffold an epic + child beads with correct assignees (no manual/LLM ticket creation).
- [ ] Worker/overseer can deterministically claim work with an "at most 1 in_progress per assignee" guard.
- [ ] `/village:work` and village work-loop prompts use the deterministic tools.
- [ ] Tests cover the deterministic selection + guard behavior.

## Notes

Key files:
- `plugins/village.ts`
- `agents/worker.md`
- `agents/overseer.md`
- `opencode.json`

title: village_claim: deterministic claim + single in_progress guard
description:
## Context

We need a deterministic way for `worker` (and `overseer`) to start work without relying on prompt-following.

Implement a new tool in `plugins/village.ts` (name suggestion: `village_claim`) that:
- checks if the assignee already has an `in_progress` bead
- if yes: returns that bead ID (do not claim a new one)
- if no: selects the next ready bead deterministically and claims it

The goal is to guarantee: at most one bead is `in_progress` per assignee when using the village flow.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/deterministic-village-workflow`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New tool exists (e.g., `village_claim`) and is usable by worker/overseer sessions.
- [ ] Tool checks `bd list --status in_progress --assignee <worker|overseer> --json`.
- [ ] If exactly one `in_progress` exists, tool returns it and does not claim a new bead.
- [ ] If more than one `in_progress` exists, tool fails loudly (returns error + list) and does not claim.
- [ ] If none are `in_progress`, tool queries `bd ready --assignee <worker|overseer> --json` and selects the next bead deterministically.
- [ ] Claim is performed via an atomic operation (`bd update <id> --claim` preferred), with actor/assignee set correctly.
- [ ] Tool output is concise (claimed/existing bead ID + title + status).

## Notes

- Prefer `execFile` (not `exec`) to avoid shell quoting issues.
- Deterministic ordering suggestion: sort by `priority` asc (0 highest), then `created_at` asc, then `id`.

comments.author: technoch1ef
comments.text: Implementation complete. Ready for review.

title: village_scaffold: deterministic epic + child bead creation
description:
## Context

Mayor currently creates epics/child beads by LLM-driven command execution, which sometimes results in missing child beads or incorrect assignees.

Add a deterministic tool in `plugins/village.ts` (name suggestion: `village_scaffold`) that creates an epic and a set of child beads with:
- correct `issue_type`, `priority`, `assignee`
- correct parent/child linkage
- consistent bead body sections (Context/Skills/Branch/Acceptance/Notes)

This should be implemented in code (tool execute), not as a prompt template.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/deterministic-village-workflow`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New tool exists (e.g., `village_scaffold`).
- [ ] Tool accepts structured input for:
  - epic title (and optional epic body)
  - branch name
  - list of children (title, type, priority, assignee, body)
- [ ] Tool validates child assignees are only `worker` or `overseer` (or empty for epics).
- [ ] Tool creates epic first, then creates children with `--parent <epicId>`.
- [ ] Tool returns a deterministic, copy/paste-safe summary of created IDs.
- [ ] Tool has a safe failure mode (no partial silent success); if partial creation happens, it reports which IDs were created.

## Notes

- Prefer `bd create ... --json` and parse IDs.
- Consider supporting `dry_run` option that prints what would be created.

title: village_orphans: deterministic orphan/suspect assignee report (+ optional fix)
description:
## Context

Incorrect or missing assignees are a common source of workflow drift (mayor forgets to assign, assigns to a wrong string, etc.).

We currently have a `/village:orphans` command template in `opencode.json`, but it relies on LLM execution.

Implement a deterministic tool in `plugins/village.ts` (name suggestion: `village_orphans`) that reproduces the `/village:orphans` behavior:
- report unassigned (orphan) non-epic beads in open/in_progress
- report suspect assignees (not `worker`/`overseer`) for non-epics
- optionally apply a safe fix mode for *unassigned non-epics only*

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/deterministic-village-workflow`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New tool exists (e.g., `village_orphans`) with args:
  - `fix?: boolean`
  - optional `limit?: number`
- [ ] Tool runs deterministic reads:
  - `bd list --status open --json`
  - `bd list --status in_progress --json`
- [ ] Tool ignores epics for auto-fix (epics may be reported separately for observability).
- [ ] Report includes counts + a concise table: `id | title | status | assignee`.
- [ ] Fix mode assigns ONLY orphaned non-epic beads using the existing keyword heuristic (review/check -> overseer, else worker).
- [ ] Tool outputs exactly what it changed in fix mode (IDs updated).

## Notes

- This should remove reliance on LLM correctness for orphan detection and assignment.
- Keep behavior aligned with `opencode.json` `/village:orphans` description.

title: Add tests for deterministic village tools + prompt invariants
description:
## Context

We need automated coverage so the deterministic workflow doesn't regress.

Add/extend Bun tests under `tests/` to cover the new village tools and any extracted pure helpers (sorting, selection, invariant checking), plus a lightweight assertion that work-loop prompt strings reference the deterministic tool(s).

- [ ] Tests cover orphan detection heuristics if implemented in tool.
- [ ] Tests assert work-loop prompts contain references to the deterministic tool(s) (and not the old primary claim path).

## Notes

title: (Optional) Add worker guardrail: prevent manual multi-claim
description:
## Context

Even with deterministic tools, the worker can still manually run `bd update ... --status in_progress` and accidentally claim multiple beads.

Add a guardrail in worker permissions/instructions to strongly prefer the deterministic claim tool and reduce the chance of multi-claim.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

`epic/deterministic-village-workflow`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Worker guidance clearly states that claiming must be done via the deterministic tool (e.g., `village_claim`).
- [ ] Worker bash permissions are adjusted to block or require confirmation for direct `bd update ... in_progress` claiming commands (while still allowing handoff/status updates).
- [ ] Document the exact allowed/denied patterns and a recovery path if the guardrail blocks a legitimate action.

## Notes

- Keep this safe: don't block common non-claim updates like handoff to overseer (`--assignee overseer --status open`) or marking blocked.

title: opencode: ensure generated shell snippets never contain literal \n tokens
description:
## Context
Some multi-command snippets produced by agents get pasted into shells with literal `\n` tokens between commands (e.g. `; \nbd create ...`). In zsh/bash, `\n` is treated as backslash-escaped `n`, so `\nbd` becomes the command `nbd` and fails (`command not found: nbd`).

We want the tool/agent output to be copy-paste safe: use real newlines (or `;` separators) and never emit literal `\n` tokens in command blocks.

## Skills
- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch
`epic/opencode-shell-snippets`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shell snippets emitted by prompts/templates are copy-paste safe (no literal `\n` before a command)
- [ ] Regression coverage (unit/snapshot/e2e) for multi-command snippet formatting
- [ ] Docs/FAQ mention the pitfall and the safe patterns

## Notes
Workaround today: delete the `\n` tokens or paste with real line breaks.

title: Village delegation observability
description:
## Context

The `village_spawn` tool creates worker/overseer sessions as *child sessions* of the current root session. In practice, many users don't realize they must open the session picker to see/switch into those sessions, so it looks like "nothing is happening" while beads assignment changes in the background.

## Goal

Make delegation observable in the TUI so a mayor can quickly:
- see which village sessions exist (worker/overseer)
- jump to them
- know whether they're idle/running/errored

## Non-goals

- changing the Beads workflow semantics
- supporting multiple workers in the same git worktree beyond the existing warning

- [ ] The command template calls `village_wake` with:
  - default `target: \"all\"`

  - optional `note` (only when arguments are provided)
- [ ] Argument behavior:

title: Remove legacy /work references; use /village:work everywhere
description:
## Context

We renamed `/work` to `/village:work` and marked `/work` as deprecated. However, several docs still reference `/work` as if it's the primary command.

Found in:
- `agents/mayor.md` (lines 39, 82): tells humans to run `/work`
- `AGENTS.md` (line 14): mentions `/work` in the slash commands example
- `VILLAGE.md` (line 38): mentions `/work` as legacy but doesn't update the workflow steps to prefer `/village:work` everywhere

## Skills

- beads-workflow

## Branch

`fix/village-orphans-report`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `agents/mayor.md` references `/village:work` instead of `/work` (both occurrences).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` updates the example to use `/village:work`.
- [ ] `VILLAGE.md` workflow steps (line 28, etc.) consistently use `/village:work`.
- [ ] Keep the deprecation note in `VILLAGE.md` (line 38) but clarify it's for backward compatibility only.
- [ ] Ensure no other user-facing docs or comments reference `/work` as the primary command.

## Notes

This is a consistency/clarity cleanup. Do not remove `commands/work.md` (it should remain as the deprecated alias).
